title: Chicken Breast with Blueberry Sauce
excerpt: Pan-seared chicken breast topped with a succulent warm sauce of fresh blueberries and rosemary. A main dish full of color and contrast.
imageAlt: Sliced chicken breast topped with a sweet-and-sour sauce of fresh blueberries and rosemary on a white plate.

ingredients.text: Sea salt and black pepper, to taste

steps: Pat the chicken breast fillets dry with paper towels and season them generously on both sides with sea salt and ground black pepper.
Heat the olive oil in a wide skillet over medium-high heat. Sear the chicken breasts for 6 minutes per side until cooked through and well browned outside.
Move the chicken to a plate and loosely cover it with aluminum foil so it rests and keeps all its inner juices.
In the same skillet over medium heat, melt the butter and sauté the chopped garlic with the rosemary sprig for 1 minute, stirring constantly so it doesn’t burn.
Pour in the chicken broth, lemon juice and honey, scraping the bottom of the skillet with a wooden spatula to lift the concentrated flavors from the browning of the chicken.

Add the Fresh Pick blueberries, picked in the mountains of Guasca, whose natural balance of tartness and sweetness gives the sauce the perfect body. Cook over gentle heat for 4 to 5 minutes, gently pressing half of the berries with a wooden spoon to release their juice and leaving the rest whole.
Slice the chicken breast on the diagonal, serve it on plates and pour the warm blueberry sauce over the top before enjoying.
tips: Don’t crush all the blueberries when making the sauce; leaving several whole gives a pleasant texture and a juicy burst in every bite of chicken.

Keep Fresh Pick blueberries in the fridge in their original container, unwashed; wash them only under a gentle stream of cold water right before using them to keep their natural protective bloom intact.
